findings.title: Unbounded job admission and retention permit resource exhaustion
findings.description: The service uses an unbounded channel and an unbounded dictionary for review jobs. Every accepted job is retained in `runs`, including terminal jobs, while `RecentRunLimit` only limits query results and does not remove entries. A caller able to submit many otherwise valid reviews can continually increase queued work, retained manifests, progress and observation state, and durable run data, eventually exhausting process memory or repository storage. Expensive estimation and file hashing occur before admission, so queue consumer concurrency does not bound request-side resource consumption.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded channel with explicit backpressure or rejection, enforce per-repository and per-caller limits on queued and active reviews, and rate-limit preflight/enqueue operations. Evict terminal work items from `runs` after a defined retention period and retrieve historical results from a bounded or paginated durable store. Apply admission checks before expensive estimation and hashing.
